title: Burst capacity gap during tenant-weighted scaling causes customer latency spikes
creator: Sana Patel
description: Customer (OmniRetail) reported repeated 5–15s tail latencies for inference during scheduled regional maintenance windows. Investigation indicates autoscaler failed to provision burst capacity despite available reserved GPUs; requests were queued and rate-limited leading to customer escalations and support SLO breaches.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy tenant with tenant_weight=2.5 and burst_policy=enabled
2) Simulate 3x normal request rate with varied sequence lengths skewed to medium (256 tokens)
3) Trigger scheduled node maintenance in region to force partial capacity eviction
4) Observe autoscaler decision logs and queued_requests metric
investigation_summary: Initial traces show autoscaler relied on instantaneous throughput metric (tokens/s) and ignored pending_queue_pressure when tenant_weight >1. Autoscaler heuristics used a decayed average window that was biased by recently completed cached-prefix requests, underestimating demand. A code change in autoscaler v1.42 (PR #4127) introduced a optimization that skipped evaluating queued_requests for tenants with cached-prefetch enabled; this path was not covered by integration tests.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed: reverted cached-prefetch skip (PR #4239) and rolled autoscaler to previous stable node group for affected region. Short-term config change applied: increase burst_pool_headroom from 10% to 30% for tenants with tenant_weight>1. Support notified customers and applied rate-limiting exemptions for active critical customers.

postmortem_actions: 1) Add integration tests covering tenant_weight >1 with cached-prefetch enabled
2) Add alert on queued_requests/allocated_capacity > 0.2 for >5m for reserved pools
3) Add unit tests for autoscaler path that skipped queued evaluation
4) Run failure injection test in staging for scheduled maintenance scenarios
5) Publish runbook updates and notify SRE rotations

2) Complete integration tests and include in CI gating (owner: Sana Patel, estimate 3)

5) Evaluate long-term capacity model changes to account for tenant_weight heterogeneity
